ai_assessment.method: Full direct Japanese-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 15 canonical passages and both titles. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported 2 major and 12 minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.55; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: Kandata’s howled order had been punctuated with Vietnamese full stops copied from 。, which made it sound calm. Exclamation marks now match the narrated 喚きました.
針の山 had been capitalised núi Kim, readable as a proper name or Sino-Vietnamese 金 (gold). Now núi chông kim at first mention and lowercase núi kim thereafter (2.1, 2.2, 2.5).
しめた rendered as the triumphant “Hay rồi! Hay rồi!” instead of the flat Được rồi; the narrator’s surprise marker ではございませんか restored as có lạ không chứ!, mirroring 2.2.
The closing time sentence now mirrors 1.1 (“chắc hẳn lúc ấy… gần trưa”), restoring the frame symmetry of morning and noon.
後には is temporal; replaced spatial Phía sau with Rồi chỉ còn lại and the faintly comic ngắn ngủn with buông thõng một đoạn ngắn.
〜のでございましょう is conjectural: Ấy là vì became Có lẽ vì; the paragraph again opens with Kandata as its topic.
浅間しく思召された now carries both pity and shame (đáng thương mà cũng thật đáng hổ thẹn); じっと rendered chăm chú.
Removed a misattached simile (cái miệng to như một thằng ngốc) and rephrased as há hốc miệng ra như một thằng ngốc.
Lúc nhúc describes a teeming crowd, not one man; removed.
Smoothed the thread’s descent: một sợi mảnh mai lấp lánh, cứ thế êm êm trôi xuống for するすると.
Vietnamese storyteller markers approximate but cannot reproduce the honorific spoken texture of 〜でございます and 御〜になる; some politeness is carried only by Đức Phật/Ngài.
The dateline keeps the Taishō era form (năm Đại Chính thứ 7) without a Gregorian gloss (1918), which belongs in apparatus rather than the text.

summary: Full assessment of all 15 Japanese/Vietnamese passages and both titles. The Buddha’s morning walk, the view through the pond to hell, Kandata’s crimes and single mercy, the silver thread, the blood pool and needle mountain, the climb, the following crowd of sinners, the shout, the snap, the fall, the Buddha’s sorrow and the indifferent noon lotuses are complete and in order, with the dateline retained. Two major findings from the separate-context pass (misreadable núi Kim; shouted lines flattened by full stops) and ten minor ones were revised; the opening and closing lotus passages now mirror each other. Fidelity, imagery and mechanics are 9.0; voice and naturalness 8.5 because the honorific oral register can only be approximated. Unrounded weighted score 8.8 meets the unchanged 8.6 threshold. No unresolved major or critical issue remains.

title_review.rationale: 蜘蛛の糸 is literally ‘the spider’s thread’. Sợi tơ nhện is the plain, natural Vietnamese equivalent, matches the recurring body term exactly and reveals nothing about the outcome.
